rv.q: Like all the best theatre, Dennis Kelly’s new play, sharply directed by Lyndsey Turner, makes this command impossible to follow.
But in its every detail, Lyndsey Turner’s production is monotone and monochrome.

Riding on Dennis Kelly ’s rollercoaster monologue “Girls & Boys,” Mulligan gives a phenomenal, unpredictable solo performance — a proper feat of acting — as a woman so self-assured she might just smash the patriarchy apart single-handedly.
It deserves to be seen by a wider audience.
Kelly dresses up his narrative in ways that detract from its power
Mulligan, who deserves the highest praise for the control and variety she brings to such a harrowing part.
